Chapter Eight: Navigating Growth with Intention—Scaling What Matters
So, your company’s finally found its stride. And now, that big question pops up: How do we grow from here?
You’ve probably heard the usual advice—bigger is always better, right? But what if there’s more to it than just growing fast for the sake of it?
Intentional growth is about expanding with care. It’s about scaling what already works, while holding onto those values and that unique culture that made your business special in the first place.
Think of it like tending a bonsai tree. Growth isn’t wild or unchecked—it’s guided, shaped thoughtfully, and every new branch is given attention. So instead of just asking, “How fast can we grow?”, maybe try asking, “ Why do we want to grow, and what are we willing to change—or protect—along the way?”
Let’s break down a practical approach to growing with intention:
First, get clear on your priorities. What exactly do you want to scale? Is it revenue, your impact, the size of your team, or maybe something else entirely?
Next, protect your core values. As you bring on new people and make bigger decisions, make sure your hiring, your choices, and your customer experience all stay true to your original principles.
And don’t forget about pacing. Growing too quickly can lead to mistakes or burnout. Instead, try to expand at a pace that gives you time to learn, adapt, and keep your quality high.
One of the hardest, but most important, parts? Learning to say no. Sometimes, turning down an enticing opportunity is exactly what keeps your company healthy and in line with its mission.
Picture this: A founder decides to limit the number of new clients each quarter. Why? To make sure every customer gets the best service possible, and the team doesn’t get overwhelmed. Or maybe another founder waits to enter a new market until their systems and support structures are rock-solid.
Growing with intention also means looking ahead and preparing for the new challenges that come with scale—like more complex operations, tougher communication, and the risk of drifting away from your purpose. If you’re ready for these hurdles, and you plan ahead, you’ll navigate growth with a lot more confidence—and integrity.
So here’s the real takeaway: Scaling what matters isn’t about chasing every shiny new opportunity. It’s about building a company that stays true to its purpose, no matter how much it grows or evolves.
